evidence.claim: Cardholder C08299 denies the flagged $30.02 charge 3581141 and also the three earlier identical $30.02 charges, states they have no subscription or recurring service billing that amount, and confirms no one else has access to the card or account; they request all four be disputed and the card reissued.

Four charges of exactly $30.02 exist on this card (3342487, 3381749, 3545489, 3581141) with day gaps of 13 and 56 across 2016-10 and 2016-12; looks_monthly = false, so the amount repetition does not match any genuine monthly billing cadence and cannot be explained as a recurring merchant.

The flagged transaction is low-signal by model standards: risk_score 0.28, amount_z -0.54, amount 0.45x the 180d mean of $65.98, online/product S matching 87%/85% of history - i.e. deliberately unremarkable charges that would not trip an amount-based rule.

No rare-device link supports a ring: the flagged device string is 'unknown | unknown | unknown | unknown', a generic placeholder appearing 5 times in this card's own 180d baseline, and none of the three rare shared device profiles (12-25 cards all-time) appear on the disputed transactions.
Region 203 shows 7 newcomer cards in 7 days with 1 having fraud history (rate 0.14 vs base rate 0.10) - not a meaningful cluster, so §3a's shared-region trigger for a report is not met.

Structurally linked memory shows denials of unrecognised online charges on shared-device cards closing as confirmed fraud (CC-0241 $99.98, CC-1672 $174.92), while the cleared cases in memory all involved the cardholder CONFIRMING the purchase - the opposite of the reply here.
Policy R2 applies: customer denies the transaction, so BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE; exposure $120.08 is below $1,000 and there is no shared-device or cross-card link, so no FILE_REPORT.

case.summary: Cardholder C08299 disputed a $30.02 online charge (3581141, 2016-12-28). My first read treated it as a likely legitimate recurring charge because three earlier charges of exactly $30.02 (3342487, 3381749, 3545489) sit in the card's history. The customer_validation reply eliminates that: the cardholder does not recognise any of the four, has no subscription billing $30.02, and reports sole access to the card. With no benign recurring explanation, four identical low-value, low-scoring online charges on a card whose number appears to have been reused over two months read as card-not-present fraud. Exposure is $120.08. Recommended actions: BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE with reissue; no suspicious activity report, since exposure is under $1,000 and the only device string involved is the generic 'unknown | unknown | unknown | unknown' placeholder already present in the card's own history, not a rare shared profile.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: The cardholder states they do not recognise the three earlier $30.02 charges either and have no subscription or recurring service billing that amount; nobody else has access to the card or account. They ask that all four charges be disputed and the card reissued.

stop_reason: Verification settled the question: customer_validation -> denies (policy §6). The verification response settles the question under policy §6: the cardholder's denial of the whole $30.02 series, plus the absence of any monthly cadence, is decisive for a BLOCK_CARD/CREATE_CASE outcome, and no further request could change it.
